South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 12/10/28 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for COPD management, evaluation of renal function, and mental health reassessment.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up approximately four weeks after his last visit. He reports that although his respiratory symptoms have shown slight improvement, he still experiences significant exertional dyspnea, particularly with moderate activities such as climbing stairs or walking briskly. He continues to utilize his albuterol inhaler, now averaging five times daily, as he feels it provides temporary relief. The productive cough persists with clear sputum, and he denies any hemoptysis or recent respiratory infections.
Mr. Fairfax expresses ongoing concern regarding the bilateral lower extremity edema, which remains prominent. He notes that despite increasing the furosemide dosage to 200 mg daily, he has only experienced a modest reduction in swelling. He reports a weight gain of 1 pound since the last visit, indicating persistent fluid retention. He rates the discomfort from the edema as 6/10.
Regarding his mental health, Mr. Fairfax states that he has been feeling more anxious, particularly about his health and the impact of his physical limitations. Sleep disturbances continue to be a significant issue, with difficulty falling asleep and frequent awakenings. He has attended cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions but feels that additional support may be necessary.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, no fevers or chills. Pulmonary - + exertional dyspnea, + productive cough, + wheezing, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - + increased anxiety, + insomnia, no dizziness or headaches.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) 2. Hypertension 3. Osteoarthritis 4. Persistent fatigue 5. Anxiety and depression (ongoing management)
PAST SURGICAL HISTORY
1. Right knee arthroscopy in 2018.
FAMILY HISTORY
Father - history of lung cancer. Mother - history of hypertension.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives alone in , . Former carpenter, now retired. Quit smoking 15 years ago. Occasional alcohol use. No illicit drug use.
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
MEDICATIONS ON FOLLOW-UP
1. Albuterol inhaler as needed, currently using five times daily. 2. Lisinopril 20 mg daily. 3. Fluticasone/salmeterol 500/50 MDI, 2 puffs twice daily. 4. Tiotropium 18 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs daily. 5. Acetaminophen 500 mg as needed for pain. 6. Furosemide 200 mg daily (increased from 160 mg). 7. Sertraline 150 mg daily (no change). 8. Prednisone 40 mg daily for COPD exacerbation (completed course).
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: T 98.6F, HR 76, BP 130/80, RR 22, O2 sat 86% on room air.
General: Elderly male in mild respiratory distress, appears fatigued but cooperative. HEENT: No nasal congestion, oropharynx clear. Pulmonary: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally, moderate wheezing noted on expiration, no crackles. Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: 2+ pitting edema in bilateral lower extremities, no erythema or warmth.
LABORATORY DATA
1. CBC: WBC 8.9, Hgb 11.0, Hct 32.0, Plt 215. 2. BMP: Na 135, K 4.5, Cl 100, CO2 23, BUN 40, Cr 2.5, Glucose 92. 3. BNP: 650 (elevated). 4. Thyroid function tests: TSH 2.4 (within normal limits).
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. COPD management: Mr. Fairfax's respiratory status shows slight improvement; however, the exertional dyspnea persists. An updated pulmonary function test is scheduled for next week to further evaluate lung function. Consideration for a change in bronchodilator therapy may still be warranted if symptoms do not improve. 2. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril. The serum creatinine has stabilized but remains elevated, indicating ongoing renal impairment. Nephrology will be consulted for further evaluation and management. 3. Lower extremity edema: The edema remains significant despite increased diuretic therapy. Reinforce dietary sodium restrictions and continue furosemide at 200 mg daily. Daily weight monitoring remains essential, and nephrology follow-up will be pursued. 4. Mental health: Mr. Fairfax will continue with sertraline at 150 mg daily. A referral to psychiatry for medication management will be expedited due to increased anxiety and insomnia. Continued engagement in cognitive-behavioral therapy is encouraged.
Patient education reiterated regarding the importance of recognizing exacerbation signs, adherence to medication, and lifestyle modifications to effectively manage COPD and edema.
